title: The Doctrine of the Holy Crown and Unwritten Constitutionalism

sections.title: The Structural Mechanism
sections.content: Unlike post-revolutionary France or the United States, Hungary did not possess a single written constitution until 1949. Instead, like Great Britain, it operated under a *történeti alkotmány* (Historic Constitution) composed of fundamental statutes and centuries of customary law (*szokásjog*).

sections.title: Rhetorical Application & Stance
sections.content: Central to this system was the *Szent Korona-tan*: the Holy Crown was not an object of jewelry, but a juristic person representing the state, uniting monarch and nation (*a korona tagjai*).
